what: Keep a discarded workout for about 10 seconds with an Undo bar, instead of wiping it the moment 'Discard workout?' is confirmed
why: A mis-tap on the confirm loses a whole live workout for good; the saved copy is cleared in the same step
impact_why: Rare, but it costs the member an hour of logging and their trust in the app
my_view: My view: do it; the app already shows Undo bars for deleted sets and routine swaps, so it is the same pattern on one more button.

what: Offer Undo after deleting a routine or a whole folder (a folder takes every routine inside it with it)
why: Today a folder delete removes all its routines at once after one question, with no way back; a member who built a 4-day plan by hand loses all of it
impact_why: Routines are the member's own work; losing them is the kind of mistake that ends a habit
my_view: My view: do it for folders first (the bigger loss); routines can follow with the same snapshot-and-restore code.

what: Make the plan builder start from the member's last answers (days, split, minutes, equipment, sore spots), not from the defaults each time
why: Every start resets to 3 days, 60 minutes, gym equipment; only goal and level come from the profile, so a member rebuilding their plan after 8 weeks answers all 5 steps again
impact_why: Saves 4 or 5 taps on a screen used every few weeks
my_view: My view: do it; keep the answers on the phone with the rest of the workout settings, and still let the member change any step.

what: Remember the exercise picked under Progress, Your lifts, 'Any exercise' after the app restarts
why: The pick is kept in memory only; after a restart Progress jumps back to the most-trained lift, so a member following one lift (for example Deadlift) picks it again every time
impact_why: Small, but it is on the screen members open to see progress
my_view: My view: do it; one saved value, cleared if that exercise is merged or removed.

what: Let the gym set its plates and bars once in the panel, and give that setup to every member of the gym as the starting plate calculator setup
why: Today each member sets up the gym's plates and bars on their own phone; most never do, so the plate calculator assumes standard plates the gym may not have
impact_why: A small 'your gym knows its own kit' moment for every member, and a reason for the owner to open the panel
my_view: My view: worth doing after the busier gym features; the member's own change should still win over the gym's setup.

what: When a member joins or moves to a new gym, ask once: 'New gym, new machines? Start machine and cable records fresh from today' and apply it to those exercises in one go
why: 'Start records fresh' exists but only one exercise at a time, and only from today; its own notes name 'a new gym, a new machine' as the reason, yet a member moving gyms would have to do it on every machine exercise
impact_why: Machine weights differ between gyms; without this the new gym's first weeks show fake 'worse than before' numbers
my_view: My view: do it as a single optional question on the join screen; free weights (barbell, dumbbell) stay untouched.

what: Suggest duplicate exercises to merge: an own exercise whose name matches a library exercise or one of its other names, for example after an import from Hevy or Strong
why: Merging works, but the member has to find duplicates by hand; an import from another app is the moment most duplicates appear
impact_why: Duplicates split one lift's history and records in two, which makes the charts look flat
my_view: My view: do it as a quiet 'Possible duplicates' line on the Exercises list; never merge without the member's tap, since a merge cannot be undone.

what: When a member keeps changing the rest on one exercise to the same length (for example 3 workouts in a row skipping to 1:30 on curls), offer 'Make 1:30 the rest for curls?'
why: The per-exercise rest is only set by hand; members rarely find that setting, so the timer keeps ringing at the wrong time
impact_why: Fewer interruptions in every workout for members who never open the settings
my_view: My view: maybe later; useful, but behind the ideas above, and it must ask once, never change the rest by itself.
